q: What is a probationary period at a new job?
r: An early period when performance is reviewed closely
It tests fit.
w: A period when the employee is not paid
A period when the employee cannot be reviewed
A paid vacation for new hires

q: What is job security?
r: The likelihood that a person will keep their job
Stable industries offer more.
w: A guard who protects an office

q: Which is more likely to provide steady income: a salaried office job or seasonal freelance work?
r: A salaried office job
Pay is regular and predictable.

q: What is a paycheck stub used for?
r: Checking how gross pay became net pay
It lists deductions.

q: A phone costs $600 new or $420 refurbished with a warranty. Which is the better value if both meet your needs?
r: The refurbished phone

w: It costs more for the same need.

q: What is a rebate?
r: A partial refund after you buy a product
You usually must submit a form.

q: A $200 item has a $30 mail-in rebate. What is your final cost if you claim it?
r: $200 minus $30 equals $170.

q: Why read reviews before a major purchase?
r: They give experiences of real buyers
Patterns can reveal problems.
w: They remove the need to compare

q: Which review is most useful?
r: A detailed review explaining what worked and what did not
It gives specifics.
w: A review that says Worst ever

q: What is a refund?
r: Money returned to a buyer for a returned or cancelled purchase

q: What is a savings account's APY?
r: The yearly return including compounding
It helps compare accounts.
w: The yearly fee for owning the account

r: $30 minus $22 equals $8.

q: What is a money market account?
r: A deposit account that often pays more than regular savings but limits transactions
It blends savings and checking features.
w: A stock account for buying shares

q: What is a minimum balance requirement?
r: The least amount you must keep in an account to avoid fees

w: The most you can keep in an account

q: Your account requires a $500 minimum balance or charges $10 a month. Your balance is often $300. What is the yearly fee?
r: $10 x 12 months equals $120.

q: What is an overdraft?
r: Spending more than the balance in a checking account
Fees may apply.

q: Which habit best helps avoid overdraft fees?
r: Tracking your balance and setting low-balance alerts
Awareness prevents overdrafts.

q: What is direct deposit?
r: Paying wages straight into a bank account
It is fast and safe.

q: What is a credit inquiry?
r: A lender's request to view your credit report

w: A request to cancel a card

q: You apply for six credit cards in one month. What is the likely effect?
r: Several hard inquiries that may lower your score
Many applications signal risk.

q: What is a late payment's effect on credit?
r: It can lower your score and stay on your report for years
Payment history matters most.

q: A bill is due on the 5th. Which habit best prevents late payments?
r: Setting up automatic payments or reminders
Automation prevents misses.

q: What is an annual fee on a credit card?
r: A yearly charge for holding the card
Some cards have none.
w: A reward for using the card

q: A card charges a $95 annual fee and gives $120 in rewards a year. Is it worth it?
r: Yes, by about $25
$120 minus $95 equals $25.

q: What is an introductory APR?
r: A temporary low rate offered when you open a card
It later rises to the regular rate.
w: A fee for opening a card

q: What should you check about an introductory 0% APR offer?
r: When it ends and what the regular rate becomes

w: Only the color of the card

q: What does a health insurance deductible reset on?
r: The start of each plan year

w: Each time you visit a doctor

q: Why might a high-deductible health plan suit a healthy young adult?
r: Lower premiums, with an account to save for costs
They rarely need much care.
w: It pays for everything with no cost

q: What is a generic drug?
r: A medicine with the same active ingredients as a brand-name drug, usually cheaper
It saves money.
w: A medicine with no active ingredient

q: What is preventive care?
r: Health services that help prevent illness, such as vaccines and screenings
Many plans cover it.
w: A fee for visiting a specialist

q: Why can preventive care save money?
r: Catching problems early often costs less than treating advanced illness
Prevention reduces costly care.

q: What is a policyholder?

w: The company that issues the policy
A person who files a lawsuit

q: What is a beneficiary?
r: The person who receives insurance or account proceeds when the owner dies

w: The person who pays the premium
The person who sells the policy

q: Why should you review your beneficiaries after a major life change?
r: So proceeds go to the people you intend
Marriage or a new child may change wishes.
w: Because the insurer requires you to change them yearly

q: What is a rental car insurance waiver?
r: Optional coverage for damage to a rental car

w: A fee for returning a car late

q: What is a prospectus?
r: A document describing an investment's goals, fees and risks
Read it before investing.

q: Which section of a fund's prospectus helps you compare costs?
r: The fee and expense table
It shows the expense ratio.

q: What is a bond rating?
r: An assessment of the issuer's ability to repay

w: The interest rate set by the Federal Reserve

q: Which bond is generally the lowest risk?
r: A bond rated AAA
The top rating signals strong credit.
w: An unrated bond from an unknown firm

q: What is a stock's ticker symbol?
r: A short code that identifies a listed company
For example, a company may have a three- or four-letter code.

q: What does an investor's cost basis mean?
r: The original price paid for an investment

w: The price at which it is sold
